dedupe_keys.name: punjab pakistan provincial drainage upgrade and urban flooding in the july 2026 monsoon

description: This Arab News Pakistan report of 23 July 2026 covers claims by Punjab's government that a large drainage upgrade reduced urban flooding during heavy monsoon rain. The province reports investing 500 billion rupees, about 1.8 billion dollars, raising functional underground water storage tanks from 5 to 41, using about 1,000 machines and desilting 700 to 750 open drains between 30 May and mid-June, removing 650,000 tonnes of solid waste. The housing and local government minister said that after 150 mm of rain in Lahore's Laxmi Chowk area water cleared within 80 to 85 minutes, whereas neighbourhoods used to stay flooded for days. Rainfall that week reached 245 mm in Gujranwala, 123 mm in Lahore, 139 mm in Sialkot and 138 mm in Mandi Bahauddin. The article is free to read and states no licence. The source is a web article available online. Caveats: the results are the government's own statements at a press conference with no independent measurement, and no models are described. For simulation, it offers a policy case for capacity planning and climate adaptation of urban drainage.
